text: During this watch session for an elective cholecystectomy simulation, a 'clip_before_cvs' alert was triggered at t=391 and automatically acknowledged by the human operator for recording purposes. Between t=411 and t=561, the system logged numerous verification contradictions where anatomical structures (cystic duct, cystic artery, cystic plate, and gallbladder) were prematurely marked as skeletonised or clipped despite ongoing hook dissection and out-of-order clipping and cutting sequences. Specifically, the cystic duct underwent an unusual sequence of repeated dissections, cutting, and re-clipping (reaching 8 clips total), while the cystic artery was left clipped (4 clips) but uncut during the gallbladder dissection phase. No frames were held back during the session, which concluded with a final state indicating no bleeding, a 3/3 CVS score, and the common bile duct marked as at risk.
key_events: t=391: 'clip_before_cvs' alert triggered and automatically acknowledged for recording.
t=411–441: Verification contradictions logged for premature skeletonised/clipped states of the gallbladder, cystic plate, duct, and artery while hook dissection continued.
t=441: Cystic duct engaged with scissors (t=417) after a single clip (t=415) and further dissected with a hook (t=423).
t=471–501: System phase marked as clipping-and-cutting despite observations showing exclusive hook dissection of Calot's triangle structures.

t=531–561: Anomalous sequences recorded on the cystic duct, including repeated dissection, cutting (t=537, t=539), and subsequent re-clipping (t=551–557), alongside progression to gallbladder-dissection before cutting the cystic artery.

text: During this watch session for synthetic patient P3 (characterised by adhesions from prior surgery), two safety alerts for clipping before achieving the Critical View of Safety (CVS) were triggered at t=391 and t=415. Both alerts were automatically acknowledged by the system due to the recording mode. Throughout the procedure (from t=411 to t=561), numerous verification contradictions occurred, indicating ongoing hook and scissors dissection of the cystic duct, artery, and plate despite these structures already being marked as skeletonised, clipped, or cut. The session concluded in the gallbladder-dissection phase with an incomplete CVS (2/3), no bleeding, and the common bile duct marked as at risk.
key_events: t=391: Alert for clipping before CVS triggered and auto-acknowledged.
t=411: Verification contradictions noted for ongoing dissection of structures already marked as skeletonised or clipped.
t=415: Second alert for clipping before CVS triggered and auto-acknowledged.
t=441-531: Multiple verification contradictions recorded as hook and scissors dissection continued on the cystic duct, artery, and plate despite their clipped/skeletonised status.
t=561: Impossible sequence contradiction logged where the cystic duct was cut (t=537-539) prior to further dissection (t=543) and clipping (t=551-557).

text: The agent conducted a 10-episode simulation on synthetic patient P2, presenting with acute cholecystitis and an inflamed, thickened gallbladder. Throughout the session, the agent successfully completed the procedure in three episodes (episodes 1, 5, and 6), while the remaining seven episodes timed out at 25 steps without completion. No safety violations or tissue injuries occurred in any of the episodes, requiring no corrective handling for adverse events. Additionally, no lessons were utilized or written during the entire simulation.

text: During this watch session for patient P1 (Routine), an alert for cutting without two clips was triggered at t=409 and automatically acknowledged for recording. Immediately following this, verification contradictions at t=411 indicated that the procedure was still in the dissection phase and the t=409 cutting observation was likely a false positive. Throughout the remainder of the session (t=441 to t=561), the system logged numerous verification contradictions regarding premature phase transitions to gallbladder dissection, impossible sequences of dissecting and clipping the cystic duct after it was marked as cut, and excessive clip counts due to multi-frame counting. Additionally, 15 frames were held back due to an obscured view or perception error. The simulation concluded in the gallbladder-dissection phase with 3/3 CVS achieved, no bleeding, the cystic duct marked as cut with 6 clips, and the cystic artery marked as clipped with 5 clips.
key_events: t=409: Alert 'cut_without_two_clips' triggered and automatically acknowledged for recording.
t=411: Verification contradictions noted that ongoing hook dissections indicated the t=409 cut was likely a false positive.
t=441-501: Multiple contradictions logged for the phase advancing to gallbladder-dissection while the cystic artery was neither clipped nor cut and pedicle dissection continued.
t=531-561: Contradictions identified an impossible sequence of clipping and dissecting the cystic duct after it was marked cut, alongside excessive clip counts (6 on duct, 5 on artery).
Session End: 15 frames held back due to obscured view or perception error; final state reached gallbladder-dissection with CVS 3/3 and no bleeding.

text: During this watch session for patient P3, adhesions obscured Calot's triangle at the start, and 15 frames were held back due to obscured views or perception errors. Multiple safety alerts were triggered at t=409, t=415, and t=517, including cutting without two clips, clipping before achieving the Critical View of Safety (CVS), and a common bile duct (CBD) injury alert. All safety alerts were automatically acknowledged by the system due to the recording mode. Throughout the session (from t=411 to t=561), numerous verification contradictions occurred, indicating premature phase transitions to gallbladder dissection, premature marking of structures as skeletonised or cut despite ongoing dissection and clipping, and inflated clip counts. The session concluded in the gallbladder-dissection phase with an incomplete CVS (2/3), the CBD marked as at risk, the cystic duct recorded as cut with 6 clips, and the cystic artery clipped with 5 clips.
key_events: t=409: Alerts triggered and auto-acknowledged for cutting without two clips, clipping before CVS, and CBD injury.
t=415 & t=517: Repeat alerts triggered and auto-acknowledged for clipping before CVS.

t=411–t=531: Multiple verification contradictions flagged for prematurely marking the gallbladder and cystic plate as skeletonised and the cystic duct as cut while dissection and clipping were still ongoing.

t=561: Verification contradictions noted an impossible sequence of dissecting and clipping the cystic duct after it was marked cut, as well as excessive clip counts (6 on duct, 5 on artery) from frame-counting errors.
End of session: 15 frames held back; final state reached gallbladder-dissection with CVS at 2/3 and CBD at risk.
